column1: community|People living in the same area or sharing an interest.|The community centre offers activities for all ages.
council|A local authority responsible for public services.|Contact the council about household waste collection.
public service|A service provided for the benefit of the community.|The library is an important public service.
facility|A place or piece of equipment provided for a particular purpose.|The sports facility has changing rooms and lockers.
library|A place where books and other resources can be borrowed.|The library opens late on Thursdays.
librarian|Someone who manages or helps people use a library.|Ask the librarian to help you find the training guide.
borrow|To use something temporarily and then return it.|Members can borrow six books at a time.
loan|An arrangement allowing temporary use of an item.|The standard book loan lasts three weeks.
renew|To extend an arrangement for another period.|You can renew your library books online.
overdue|Not returned or completed by the required time.|An overdue book may prevent further borrowing.
due date|The date by which something must be returned or completed.|The due date is printed on your library receipt.
reservation list|A list of people waiting to borrow a particular item.|Your name has been added to the reservation list.
catalogue|A searchable list of available items.|Use the catalogue to find books on job applications.
exhibition|A public display of objects or information.|The museum exhibition explores the history of local housing.
museum|A place displaying objects of cultural or historical interest.|The museum offers free entry on Sunday mornings.
gallery|A space where works of art are displayed.|The gallery runs painting workshops for beginners.
leisure centre|A public building providing sport and recreation facilities.|You can join an exercise class at the leisure centre.
swimming pool|A specially built area of water for swimming.|The swimming pool is reserved for lessons until noon.
gym|A place with equipment for physical exercise.|Complete an induction before using the gym.
sports hall|An indoor space for sport and exercise.|The sports hall can be hired by local groups.
playing field|An outdoor area used for organised sport.|The playing field is closed after heavy rain.
playground|An outdoor area with equipment for children.|Children must be supervised in the playground.
park|Public land used for recreation.|Dogs must be kept on leads in this park.
recreation|Activities done for enjoyment during free time.|The centre provides low-cost recreation for families.
club|A group organised around a shared activity or interest.|The walking club welcomes new members.
society|An organised group sharing a particular interest.|The local history society meets once a month.
association|A group formed to represent or support shared interests.|The residents' association is discussing parking problems.
volunteer|Someone who helps without expecting pay.|Each volunteer receives basic safety training.
voluntary|Done by choice rather than because it is required.|Participation in the clean-up is voluntary.
charity|An organisation that helps people or supports a cause.|The charity collects furniture for families moving into new homes.
donation|Money or goods given to support a cause.|A small donation helps cover the cost of materials.
fundraising|Collecting money to support an organisation or cause.|The school is holding a fundraising event for new equipment.
sponsor|A person or organisation providing support for an activity.|A local business is the main sponsor of the festival.
event|An organised occasion or activity.|The event will move indoors if it rains.
festival|A series of organised celebrations or performances.|The community festival takes place in the town square.
fair|A public event with stalls or activities.|The careers fair includes local training providers.
work party|A group meeting to complete a practical task together.|The garden work party starts at nine on Saturday.
clean-up|An organised effort to remove rubbish or dirt.|Bring gloves to the riverside clean-up.
litter|Small pieces of rubbish left in public places.|Please put litter in the bins provided.
rubbish|Things that are no longer wanted and should be disposed of.|Do not leave rubbish beside the collection point.
waste|Materials that are no longer needed or useful.|Keep food waste separate from ordinary rubbish.
recycling|Processing used materials so they can be used again.|The council provides a separate bin for recycling.
compost|Decayed organic material used to improve soil.|Garden members can collect compost from the shared area.
bin|A container for rubbish or recycling.|Place the bin beside the road before seven.
collection day|The scheduled day when waste is picked up.|Check the calendar for your revised collection day.
permit|Official permission to do a particular activity.|You need a permit to hold a market stall.
licence|Official authorisation to carry out an activity.|The council explains how to apply for a trading licence.
restriction|A limit on what is allowed.|The water restriction applies to garden hoses.
penalty|A punishment for breaking a rule.|There is a penalty for dumping rubbish illegally.
permission|Agreement allowing someone to do something.|Ask permission before displaying posters in the hall.
approval|Official agreement that something may proceed.|The group needs approval to use the public square.
public notice|An announcement intended for the community.|The public notice explains the proposed road closure.
noticeboard|A board used to display public information.|Class schedules are posted on the noticeboard.
announcement|A message giving information about a change or event.|Listen for the announcement about the delayed session.
survey|A set of questions used to collect people's views.|Please complete the survey about local transport.
questionnaire|A written set of questions for gathering information.|The questionnaire asks which facilities residents use.
election|A process in which people vote to choose representatives.|The local election takes place next month.
vote|To formally choose an option or representative.|Registered residents can vote at the community hall.
registration form|A document used to record someone's details.|Return the registration form before the first session.
identification|Documents or details proving who someone is.|Bring identification when collecting your membership card.
proof of address|A document confirming where someone lives.|A recent utility bill can serve as proof of address.
opening hours|The times when a place is open to the public.|The website lists the library's opening hours.
public holiday|A day when many workplaces and public services close.|The collection schedule changes on a public holiday.
closure notice|An announcement that a facility will be unavailable.|Read the closure notice before planning your visit.
access|The ability or permission to enter or use something.|Members have access to the reading room after registration.
step-free|Accessible without using stairs.|The new entrance provides step-free access.
ramp|A sloping surface joining different heights.|Use the ramp beside the main steps.
handrail|A rail that people hold for support.|Hold the handrail when using the stairs.
changing room|A room where people change their clothes.|Lockers are available in the changing room.
locker|A small lockable cupboard for personal belongings.|Bring a coin to use the locker.
childcare|Care of children while their parents are occupied.|Childcare is available during the morning training course.
crèche|A place providing short-term care for young children.|Book a crèche place before attending the class.
nursery|A place caring for young children before school age.|The nursery accepts children from two years old.
youth centre|A place offering activities and support for young people.|The youth centre runs a free homework club.
senior citizen|An older adult, often eligible for particular services.|A senior citizen can apply for discounted pool entry.
background check|A check of someone's history for suitability or safety.|The role requires a background check before work begins.
community spirit|A feeling of cooperation and belonging among local people.|The street clean-up strengthened community spirit.
neighbourhood watch|A local group that helps improve safety by sharing concerns.|The neighbourhood watch meeting is open to all residents.
crime prevention|Action taken to reduce the likelihood of crime.|The police will give a talk on crime prevention.
reporting|The act of telling the relevant person about an issue.|The website explains the process for reporting damaged streetlights.
local authority|An organisation governing a town or district.|The local authority manages the public swimming pool.
amenity|A useful local service or feature.|The library is an important local amenity.
archive|A collection of historical records.|The local archive contains photographs of the old railway.
landfill|A site where waste is buried.|The campaign aims to reduce waste sent to landfill.
bulky waste|Large unwanted items that need special collection.|Book a bulky waste collection for your old sofa.
bylaw|A rule made by a local authority.|A local bylaw limits noise late at night.
regulation|An official rule controlling an activity.|The venue follows the regulation on maximum occupancy.
prohibition|An official rule saying something is not allowed.|The notice explains the prohibition on open fires.
petition|A formal request supported by several people's signatures.|Residents submitted a petition for a safer crossing.
public consultation|A process of gathering community views on a proposal.|The public consultation remains open until Friday.
proposal|A suggested plan for consideration.|The proposal includes a new pedestrian bridge.
objection|A stated reason for opposing something.|Send any objection to the planning office in writing.
planning permission|Official approval for certain building work.|The extension requires planning permission.
ward|A local area represented by an elected councillor.|Our ward has two representatives on the council.
councillor|An elected member of a local council.|The councillor will attend the residents' meeting.
inclusion|Making sure people can participate and belong.|The programme promotes inclusion through accessible activities.
diversity|The presence of people with different backgrounds or characteristics.|The festival celebrates the diversity of the neighbourhood.
safeguarding|Measures intended to protect vulnerable people from harm.|All volunteers receive safeguarding training.
outreach|Work that brings services to people who may not access them.|The library outreach service visits isolated residents.
participation|Taking part in an activity or process.|The organisers encourage participation from new residents.
